summary: Cloudflare Worker connection rotation trims trailing chunks on SSE resume
description: Issue summary: Customers observe that the last few tokens (often just trailing whitespace or the final punctuation) are missing after an SSE resume when requests route through Cloudflare Workers connection rotation. Impact: Final sentence fragments are getting silently trimmed in ~8% of resumed streams for Verbata's production traffic, causing truncated answers and user-facing UI glitches (cut-off sentences). This affects live-chat workflows and any flow that relies on the terminal event to mark completion. Environment: prod-us-east, SaaS customer using Redwood hosted API through Cloudflare Workers that performs header rewrites and connection pooling. Observed on redwood-chat-medium-v1 and gptj-6b-instruct. Occurs only when Worker routes cause a connection handoff / pool shuffle during resume pacing. Steps to reproduce: 1) Start an SSE streaming request to the Redwood API from a client behind a Cloudflare Worker with HTTP/1.1 keepalive enabled. 2) Let the server stream a long response (~4000 tokens). 3) Simulate a short disconnect (network blip or Worker-script triggered restart) and then re-establish the SSE resume request using the original resume token. 4) Observe that the resumed stream completes but final 1-6 characters (often whitespace or trailing period) are missing. Observed behavior differs depending on Worker caching and connection reuse. Logs & traces: see investigation notes below for excerpts. Notes: this is not a universal client bug (some clients receive intact stream). The pattern correlates with a connection rotation where the edge terminates the previous TCP session and a new one receives the remainder chunks. It appears to be sensitive to chunk boundary alignment and Cloudflare Workers' response buffering. Customer impact: high for Verbata chat flows (enterprise), intermittent for self-serve customers. Work-around in place: recommend short-lived client-side whitespace-tolerant heuristics (append missing punctuation if last chunk doesn't end with terminal marker) and temporarily route Verbata traffic around the Worker (bypass) while engineering investigates.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a minimal Cloudflare Worker that forwards requests to our API and preserves SSE headers. 2) Start a streaming chat call that yields a multi-kilobyte response. 3) After ~60-90s of streaming, force a Worker restart or force a connection pool rotation at the edge (can be simulated by rapidly re-deploying or toggling a keepalive setting). 4) Reconnect with the client's resume token and compare the final bytes of the stream to the original. Expected: resumed stream contains full final token/punctuation. Actual: final 1-6 characters are missing ~8% of the time.

comments: 2026-03-10 — Support (Aisha): Initial report from customer: truncated final punctuation on resumed streams. Asked for request IDs and sample replay.

2026-03-10 — Customer (Verbata SRE): Attached sample request id uid-9876 and indicated it's reproducible when Worker is configured to 'keep connections warm'. Provided traffic capture and Worker script.

2026-03-11 — SRE (Marco): Reproduced locally by enabling Cloudflare Worker connection rotation simulation. Observed consistent end-offset shortfall when the edge reported a mid-stream reset and resumed onto a different backend connection. Escalating to runtime team for kernel/kafka-like chunk boundary handling. Linked SUP-4721 for historical resume issues.

2026-03-11 — Runtime Eng (Leah Chen): Hypothesis: the resume offset uses byte-aligned offsets but Cloudflare's buffering discards a small buffer on connection handoff; server believes all bytes were delivered. Adding additional validation to resume handshake to verify offsets. Working on a patch to compute checksum across final N bytes.

2026-03-12 — Support (Aisha): Informed customer of planned temporary workaround (bypass Worker) and requested permission to toggle routing for a 24h window to capture full network trace. Customer approved.
investigation_notes: Initial triage focused on client SDK and server serializer; both passed basic tests. Reproduced in controlled environment by introducing an artificial mid-stream connection tear at the edge. The serving runtime logs show expected final-chunk length, but the resumable-offset reported by the edge is 4 bytes ahead of what the backend believes was acknowledged. Hypothesis: Cloudflare Workers (or CF's connection pooling) can coalesce and forward buffered bytes in a way that transiently masks the true boundary; when a connection is shuffled, a small trailing buffer remains at the Worker which the new connection doesn't replay, leading to missing trailing bytes after resume. Investigated HTTP transfer-encoding behavior, SSE chunk framing, and client-side reassembly. No evidence of corruption within our runtime; problem appears at edge/worker boundary. A patch to add an explicit final-chunk-hash in the resume handshake is being prototyped. Related historical tickets: SUP-4721 (sse-ws-reconnects) — similar resume mismatch patterns but different trigger (proxy chunking vs worker rotation).
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation: advised customer to route around Cloudflare Worker and to apply a client-side fallback that tolerates missing trailing whitespace/punctuation. Longer-term fix: landed a server-side resume-handshake enhancement (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2891) which adds a 16-bit checksum for the last N bytes and validates offsets on resume. This allows the server to detect the mismatch and request re-delivery from the client or trigger a conservative re-fetch from origin. Rollout plan: canary in prod-us-east on 2026-03-18, full rollout ~2026-03-22 pending metrics. Follow-ups: coordinate with Cloudflare AM to validate Worker pooling semantics and update docs with known edge behaviors.
